title: Translate KV-cache outage postmortem into PRD updates and acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Summary: After the KV-cache outage on 2026-03-05 (incident INC-2026-03-05-KV), the postmortem identified three classes of product changes that must be captured in the PRD: defensive fallbacks for cache read failures, improved observability and SLOs tied to KV cache behavior, and a controlled rollout plan for the cache eviction algorithm change. This ticket translates postmortem action items into concrete PRD updates, scoped requirements, and acceptance criteria so engineering and design can implement and validate changes with clear success signals.
acceptance_criteria: Automatic fallback: if a KV-cache read path fails or exceeds 100ms, the serving runtime must transparently fall back to stateless model variant within 200ms end-to-end 95% of the time; fallback must be logged and counted as a distinct metric (runtime.kvcache.fallback.count).

SLOs: define and publish a KV-cache health SLO of 99.9% availability (read success) measured per-customer per-hour, and a 95th percentile KV-cache read latency < 30ms for production traffic measured at edge ingress. These must appear in the Console SLO page and be queryable in dashboards.

Observability: add three new telemetry signals (kv_hit_rate, kv_read_latency_ms_p95, kv_fallback_count) instrumented at request level and surfaced in Console with 1-minute granularity; traces must annotate whether a response used cached KV state.

Rollout plan: changes to the eviction algorithm must be gated behind a canary targeting 5% traffic for 24 hours, with automatic rollback on threshold breaches (increase in kv_fallback_count by >2x or errors above 0.2%). Canary must be runnable per-region and per-customer tier.

Runbook & Alerts: update runtime runbook with playbook for KV degradation and define on-call alerts: kv_hit_rate < 85% for 5m, kv_fallback_count rate > baseline by 100% for 10m, and kv_read_latency_ms_p95 > 100ms for 5m.

End-to-end tests: add regression tests that simulate cache read failure and assert fallback within 200ms and no data corruption for 10k simulated requests. Tests must run in CI and be part of the release gate for runtime-2.3.0.
Docs & SDK: document new fallback semantics and metrics in the public API docs and SDK changelog.
Security: if any telemetry includes customer identifiers, ensure telemetry follows PII minimization and KMS-encrypted transport per security guidelines; security review sign-off required before GA.
decisions: Require transparent runtime fallback rather than surfacing errors to customers to protect product SLAs and developer UX.
Adopt 1-minute telemetry granularity for Console visibility to enable faster detection without overwhelming storage quotas.
Gate eviction algorithm change behind canary by traffic percentage and region, not by full-tenant flag to reduce risk of tenant-wide regressions.
Make KV-cache metrics tenant-scoped and sampled (1%) for heavy customers to balance observability with cost.

Sync with ENG runtime owners to size changes and split work into ENG-3912 (fallback implementation) and ENG-4020 (observability & metrics).
Create Console dashboard mockups for KV metrics and SLO pages (owner: Design).
Add CI regression tests and chaos scenario for KV failure simulation (owner: ENG).
Write runbook updates and playbook steps, add to incident response runbook repository (owner: SRE).
Coordinate security review and data handling sign-off (owner: Security).
Prepare rollout canary plan and rollback criteria (owner: PM + ENG).
Update public docs and SDK changelog (owner: DevRel).
